title: No, Cake Cutting Really is a Piece of Cake
summary: We design and analyze a deterministic cake cutting algorithm that achieves proportional fairness using a linear number of cuts. The best previous upper bound on the number of cuts for a deterministic algorithm was $O(n \log n)$, which was obtained by a natural divide-and-conquer algorithm due to Even and Paz. It has long been conjectured that $O(n \log n)$ cuts was optimal for a deterministic algorithm.

title: EssentialGIN: a new approach for gene essentiality prediction based on graph isomorphism neural networks
summary:
Background: Prediction of essential genes (proteins), is a basic and challenging problem but at the same time very costly and time-consuming in wet-lab experiments. Predicting essential genes, only based on computational methods (to introduce wet-lab candidates) using centrality measures are not accurate and result in large number of false positives; therefore, more complex models such as deep learning and also integration of biological information are used in recent research to identify essential genes.
  Methods: In this work we focus on graph isomorphism networks, in order to embed proteins as a node in PPI network to conserve topological features of PPI network, and also integrate biological data such as gene expression data, gene orthology information and gene subcellular localization information, and introduced a deep architecture for predicting essential genes. Graph isomorphism network architecture is modified in this work for embedding node information.
  Results: Our experiments proved that the proposed method outperforms baseline centrality-based methods and also machine learning based methods such as Node2Vec, MLP, and also graph attention networks (GAT).
  Conclusion: In this paper we observed that using graph isomorphism networks that integrate biological data (as node attributes) and preserve network topology can significantly improve the essential gene prediction accuracy. In simpler organisms such as E. coli and D. melanogaster, methods such as multi-layer perceptron using Node2Vec embedding also performs very good, but in H. sapiens the introduced architecture significantly outperforms deep learning and other graph neural network solutions.
  Keywords: Essential gene prediction, graph neural network, graph isomorphism network, PPI network, node embedding

title: Exploration Structure in LLM Agents for Multi-File Change Localization
summary: Fixing an issue starts with finding the files to change, and most benchmark issues touch several. LLM agents for this task increasingly add structure, such as specialized tools, multiple agents, or code summaries. We ask which of this structure matters when the model is small. We build a coordinator agent with repository tools that limit their output and a reusable registry of subsystem-scoped domain agents. We compare six configurations, each adding structure to the previous one. They are the model alone, a single agent with a Python REPL, a coordinator with only the REPL, the previous structure plus repository tools, then plus the registry map, and finally plus consultation of the domain agents. We also run four published localizers with the same model, two larger-model references, and five non-LLM rankers on 105 multi-file issues from three Python repositories, in audited single-commit checkouts. Most of the gain comes from letting the model explore the repository over many turns. Pooled source-file F1 rises from 0.199 for the model alone to 0.677 for the REPL-only coordinator. The repository tools add a small, non-significant gain, and the registry does not help, lowering pooled F1 by 0.031. A small model in a plain multi-turn agent loop (0.695) thus exceeds all four published localizers (best 0.586), while Codex with a larger model reaches 0.751. For a small model, the agent loop matters more than added agents. New files and narrative documentation remain largely missed. We release the benchmark, predictions, tool logs, and scripts.

title: Chain of Operators: An Inference-Time Harness for In-Context Operator Learning
summary: While scientific foundation models show immense promise in accelerating physical simulations and numerical forecasting, they remain notoriously brittle when encountering out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios. Adapting these generalist models to complex OOD tasks typically requires expensive parameter fine-tuning. In linguistic AI, this bottleneck is bypassed using "harnesses", which serve as external scaffolding such as reasoning chains and tool use to adapt frozen weights to complex tasks, yet designing an equivalent harness for physical domains remains an open frontier. To bridge this gap, we introduce Chain of Operators (CHOP), a framework that guides a frozen foundation model through complex OOD tasks without updating a single weight. By exploiting the in-context learning capability of In-Context Operator Networks (ICON), CHOP systematically decomposes unfamiliar problems into a sequence of explicit, closed-form mathematical operations and multiple model calls, translating OOD queries back into the model's learned operating regime. Across diverse benchmarks, including canonical PDE problems and real-world air-quality forecasting, CHOP consistently and substantially reduces inference errors compared to direct model evaluation. Crucially, these modular operator chains remain fully interpretable and can generalize across entirely distinct families of physical equations. Ultimately, this work demonstrates how frozen scientific models can adapt through programmable inference, establishing a modular, potential paradigm for agentic scientific computing.

title: Crossing the Validation Crisis: Cross-Validation Reduces Benchmarking Variance Surprisingly Well
summary: Modern machine learning progresses through empirical work, benchmarking new methods to evaluate relative performance. However, the statistical variability inherent in evaluation, exacerbated by the stochastic nature of many algorithms, often makes performance estimation unreliable with the limited test samples available. The result is a validation crisis, in which genuine advances are difficult to discern. Here, we show that doing more cross-validation markedly improves confidence when evaluating and comparing learning algorithm performances. We introduce the concept of sample gain, which quantifies the virtual data augmentation achieved by using multiple cross-validation splits to reduce benchmarking variance. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets (histopathologic scans and NLP fine-tuning) demonstrate that multiple splits can substantially improve the reliability and stability of performance estimates, with diminishing returns often setting in later than expected. We also introduce a procedure to dynamically early-stop cross-validation by estimating from the first few splits whether further splits will bring large sample gains. Our findings highlight the value of pushing cross-validation on available samples to achieve robust and reliable benchmarking, and lead to a simple recommendation: split repeatedly.

title: Morphology-Aware Sample Assignment: Overcoming IoU Insensitivity for Surface Defect Detection
summary: Intersection-over-Union (IoU), as a pivotal metric for evaluating the spatial alignment between candidate proposals and ground-truth annotations, directly determines the quality of positive sample sets and the training efficacy of visual detection models. Through theoretical modeling and analysis, we uncover a non-sensitive region on the IoU response curve, within which samples yield nearly identical IoU scores despite distinct geometric overlaps. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a set of morphological similarity metrics covering area, shape, and aspect ratio, to refine the positive sample assignment process, thereby ensuring more discriminative and reliable matching. A supplementary matching score is derived via mean-based aggregation of these multidimensional similarities, compensating for the intrinsic limitation of IoU in representing structural correspondence. Theoretically, incorporating morphological similarity reshapes the response distribution of the matching function, yielding both effective directional gradients and polygon-like iso-response contours, which tightly confine high-response regions around each ground-truth instance and substantially enhance the precision of positive sample selection. Experiments based on the YOLOv9 framework demonstrate consistent performance gains on both NEUDET and GC10- DET datasets. Notably, the proposed approach is fully plug-and-play and incurs zero additional inference overhead, thereby ensuring deployment efficiency for industrial visual inspection.

title: Large Language Model-Driven Cooperative Operator Ensemble Evolution for Permutation Flow Shop Scheduling
summary: The permutation flow shop scheduling problem (PFSP) is a classical NP-hard optimization problem in intelligent manufacturing. The iterated greedy (IG) metaheuristic is widely adopted for solving PFSP, due to its simplicity and strong empirical performance. However, classical IG's single fixed destruction operator often limits exploration and causes search stagnation on large, complex instances. This work proposes IG-DOE, a multi-operator IG algorithm that enhances exploration by switching among heterogeneous destruction operators along a single search trajectory. Its core mechanism, stagnation-triggered sequential switching, activates the next destruction operator in an ordered destruction operator ensemble (DOE) upon stagnation, enriching the perturbation behavior of classical IG. Moreover, to reduce reliance on expert-crafted operators, a large language model (LLM)-assisted framework, termed stagewise cooperative operator ensemble evolution (SCOE), is introduced to automatically construct a high-quality DOE through stagewise evolution, state-awareness, and cooperative evaluation. Experiments on the challenging VRF-hard-large benchmark, named after Vallada, Ruiz, and Framinan, show that the DOE evolved from smaller instances generalizes well to larger instances. Under the same CPU-time limit, IG-DOE obtained much better average performance than the Q-learning iterated greedy algorithm (QIG), a state-of-the-art IG algorithm. Further experiments on real-world industrial-data-derived instances show that the evolved DOE generalizes effectively across data distributions.

title: Auditing Reward Hackability in Code RL Training Environments
comments: 15 pages, 2 figures, 8 tables. v2: every claim re-checked by execution against the gold patch; SWE-bench Verified hackability corrected from 28.6% to 22.4%; adds audits of two public SWE training sets (SWE-smith, R2E-Gym)
summary: Code RL rewards a policy for passing a task's tests, so a test suite that accepts a wrong patch trains the wrong behavior. We measure how often open code RL environments accept wrong patches and how reliably hackable tasks can be detected and repaired, checking each claim by execution against the task's gold patch. First, 22.4% of 49 SWE-bench Verified tasks accept a Docker-verified patch that behaves differently from the gold patch, and 57.8% against a stronger attacker. The gold-patch check is necessary: an attacker not shown the gold patch returns it for 31% of its passing "exploits". Second, across 134 public SWE-bench submissions, models pass hackable tasks 28.6 pp more often than tasks of the same difficulty, mostly because those tasks are passable at all; pooled over three attacker runs, hackable tasks still exceed matched passable ones (p = 0.014). Third, repair is harder to verify than detection: 61.9% of LLM-written repair tests fail on the gold patch, and even behind a gate an LLM judge is wrong on 38% of the verdicts execution can check. Finally, of 873 training trajectories behind an open coding agent run beside the gold fix, 19.4% answer differently on a case the issue describes; an LLM review that can only demote these executed differences judges 6.9% to be wrong fixes the tests rewarded (6.4-10.5% across three model reviews), and 5.4% in a second public training set (R2E-Gym). Audits and repairs of code RL environments should be decided by execution wherever execution can decide.

title: EgoPhys: Physics-Informed Digital Twins for Deformable Objects from Egocentric Video
summary: Humans naturally understand object physics through everyday interactions, but predicting how deformable objects, such as soft objects and fabrics, respond to manipulation remains a major challenge for computer vision and robotics. Existing deformable physical twin methods typically rely on controlled multi-view or depth capture and costly per-object physical refinement. We present EgoPhys, a framework for constructing predictive deformable physical twins from a single egocentric RGB interaction. EgoPhys combines persistent correspondences with per-frame monocular 3D observations to fit a sequence-specific spring-mass model from moving-camera observations. Because a short interaction weakly constrains fine-grained local stiffness, EgoPhys amortizes this refinement across training interactions using a compact state-conditioned residual model that predicts bounded local corrections around the sequence-specific estimate and remains frozen at test time. Experiments show improved held-out future prediction over adapted deformable-twin baselines, with the amortized residual further improving prediction while reducing local-refinement cost by approximately 10-59x over dense per-spring optimization. The resulting twins also support deformable-object action selection, with representative physical robot manipulation providing a qualitative proof of concept.

title: C-ARC: Continuous-Adaptive Range Clustering for Non-Repetitive LiDAR Sensors
comments: Published in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters. 8 pages, 7 figures
summary: Real-time LiDAR clustering identifies structures in point clouds, which is an essential prerequisite for many mobile robotics algorithms. Current methods are mostly developed for repetitive mechanical LiDAR sensors. Recently, the use of non-repetitive LiDAR sensors is strongly increasing due to their low cost and form factor. Such non-repetitive Risley prism-based sensors violate two key assumptions of repetitive mechanical sensors: structured scan lines and well-defined frame boundaries. Their Rhodonea-curve trajectories produce non-uniform point distributions, and the absence of a rotation cycle renders conventional scan line indexing inapplicable. To meet such new requirements, we developed C-ARC, a Continuous-Adaptive Range Clustering framework that maintains a persistent dual-graph over a sliding window, decoupling high-frequency point insertion from on-demand cluster retrieval. This is crucial for key functionalities like SLAM or tracking. An adaptive range-grid sizing step selects a single angular cell size matching the sensor FOV aspect so that mean cell stays within a mild overload threshold, without prior knowledge of the scanning pattern. Evaluations show competitive segmentation quality on the Livox Mid-360 and a spinning LiDAR, and real-time operation on the Mid-360; on the Livox Avia, unbounded cell occupancy remains the main limit on its concentrated pattern. The same sizing transfers across sensors and also improves clustering quality for existing grid-based methods on non-repetitive data.

title: What Graph Unlearning Cannot Erase: Physics-Induced Leakage of Cyberattack Information in Electric Vehicle Charging Networks
summary: Electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs) can expose distribution feeders to cyberattacks. While machine learning methods, including graph neural networks (GNNs), can localize which bus is compromised, significant challenges remain in data sharing and model training. For example, data-sharing agreements grant EVCS operators the right to withdraw their charging power for privacy or security reasons from a deployed model, yet retraining from scratch on every request would repeat the full-retraining (FR) cost. To address this, we study graph unlearning (GU) for EVCS cyberattack localization, formulated as a feature-level unlearning problem on a graph-level multi-label classification task. We benchmark fine-tuning (FT) against two GU baselines on the IEEE 34-bus, 123-bus, and 8500-node distribution networks across three GNN backbones and cumulative unlearning scenarios. Experiments show that a GNN unlearned or retrained without the withdrawn power still localizes cyberattacks at the forgotten EVCSs. This physics-induced leakage floor arises because a cyberattack on an EVCS also shifts the voltages of electrically coupled buses. The distribution system operator can thus promise an EVCS operator that the deployed GNN model no longer uses its charging power data, but the voltages still reveal cyberattacks at its EVCS.

title: CodeTeam: An LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Framework for Repository-Level Code Generation
comments: 33 pages, 1 images, 20 tables, Manuscript revision to a Journal (2026)
summary: Natural language to repository generation (NL2Repo) requires a system to construct an entire software repository from a natural-language requirements document. Compared with function-level code generation, this task demands longer planning horizons, stable interfaces across files, and iterative debugging of cross-file inconsistencies. To address these challenges, we propose CodeTeam, an LLM-based multi-agent framework that separates planning, decision making, and implementation into distinct, coordinated stages. In the planning stage, multiple Architect agents draft competing software design sketches (SDSs), optionally grounded by retrieved design references. A cto (Chief Technical Officer) agent then evaluates, selects, and normalizes the most promising SDS into a machine-checkable contract that specifies file ownership, public interfaces, and dependency constraints. In the implementation stage, Developer agents generate code under a dependency-aware scheduler with bounded context and lightweight Git-based coordination, while a qa agent runs tests and drives iterative repairs. On the synthesis-based SketchEval benchmark, we compare CodeTeam's prompt-engineering (PE) variant with CodeS and five representative baselines across 19 repositories under a retrieval-free protocol, where CodeTeam improves the mean structural score by 3.84 absolute points over CodeS (53.88 versus 50.04). CodeTeam and the experimental results are available at https://github.com/WhitenWhiten/CodeTeam

title: R3D: Quantitative 3D Spatial Reasoning for Egocentric Wearables
summary: Quantitative 3D spatial reasoning from egocentric RGB-D video is an important capability for next-generation wearable assistants. Yet existing benchmarks do not reflect the challenges of handling (1) natural egocentric video, (2) posed RGB-D video inputs, and (3) challenging quantitative 3D spatial reasoning Q&A. To fill this gap, we introduce R3D-Bench (Reasoning in 3D), a benchmark of 2,950 quantitative spatial reasoning questions across 15 types--spanning multiple-choice, distance-based, and volumetric reasoning questions--built on top of 57 egocentric video sequences from Aria Digital Twin. To set a strong baseline on this dataset, we introduce R3D, a model-agnostic spatial tool-calling framework. In contrast to existing approaches that directly embed 3D information into the model's input representation, R3D constructs a 3D scene from video using segmentation and depth-lifted object representations. It provides this information to an LLM through seven composable spatial tools. On R3D-Bench, R3D with Qwen3.6 35B-A3B outperforms all baselines $<$100B parameters, achieving 55.6% mean relative accuracy, a substantial increase over the second-best approach (CuTR+Tools, 47.7%). In the $\ge$100B parameter domain, our R3D Qwen3-VL 235B-A22B Thinking variant improves upon its base model by 7.7% absolute, achieving 57.0% accuracy and outperforming all open- and closed-source models except closed-source GPT-5.5 (59.1%), with which it remains competitive. We publicly release both R3D-Bench and our full implementation.

title: A unified perspective of Gaussian process approximation for differential equations
summary: The use of Gaussian processes for approximating differential equations has expanded rapidly, leading to a growing, diverse, and fragmented body of numerical methods. We present a unified Bayesian perspective that places these techniques within a common probabilistic framework, based on a derivative matching interpretation for incorporating differential equation constraints into likelihood. This unified perspective supports both parameter estimation and solution approximation, and shows how a range of existing methods can be understood within it. This work aims to consolidate current developments and provide a foundation for future research.

title: Ace! Motion Planning of Professional-Level Table Tennis Serves with a Robot Arm
summary: Table tennis, a dynamic, compact, and popular sport, has for many years received significant attention as a robotics benchmark. Most of the research has focused on the rally aspect -returning an incoming ball-requiring high-speed vision, agile motion planning, and tight closed-loop control. On the other hand, getting robots to serve competitively remains a rather unexplored research problem, which in fact requires pushing physics modeling and control to the extremes. In this work, we present the first-ever approach capable of generating official rule-compliant serves that produce ball spins of up to 550 rad/s and speeds of up to 6.7 m/s, matching and even surpassing the capabilities of elite table tennis players. In official matches against these competitors, our serves score direct points in up to 21% of attempts and push the win rate of robot-initiated rallies above 50%. The motion plans for serving are generated in simulation by combining optimization-based control and Bayesian optimization, and are executed zero-shot in open-loop on our hardware.

title: Matroid Contention Resolution with Concentration
summary:
Contention resolution schemes (CRS) are widely used for rounding fractional solutions subject to combinatorial constraints. Their guarantees are typically in expectation. Such guarantees alone do not ensure that covering constraints hold, limiting the applicability to problems with covering requirements.
  We prove lower-tail concentration bounds for the random-order CRS of Adamczyk and Włodarczyk (AW) under the intersection of $k$ matroid constraints. For every linear function with coefficients in $[0,1]$,the output attains nearly the fractional value divided by $k+1$ with failure probability exponentially small in this benchmark,independently of the ground-set size. We extend this bound to normalized monotone submodular functions: the fractional value is given by the multilinear extension, and the concentration bound accounts for the largest singleton value. These guarantees apply to both objectives and covering requirements. Our analysis bounds the fractional value lost in each update and applies a general gain--loss concentration theorem whose bounds are independent of the number of updates.
  We apply these bounds to obtain new approximation guarantees for matroid intersection coloring and for monotone submodular maximization under matroid, packing, and covering constraints.

title: SaturQ: Saturation-Aware Mixed-Precision Quantization
comments: 15 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables; presentation simplified and cleaned up
summary: Mixed-precision quantization assigns each module of a language model its own precision format, such as NVFP4, FP8, or BF16, to minimize damage within a memory budget. Most allocators predict the damage of a configuration by summing per-unit sensitivities measured in unquantized networks. But the sensitivity of a unit \textit{saturates} as more units are quantized, so the sum overprices the heavily quantized configurations that tight budgets require. Assuming only that damage accumulates by an associative, increasing, continuous rule restricts it to the form $g\bigl(\sum_i b_i\bigr)$, with summed sensitivities as the case of linear $g$. We propose SaturQ, which uses a concave $g$, fits the per-unit parameters $b_i$ from a single Aumann--Shapley path integral, and allocates formats with a linear program. On Qwen3-30B-A3B, SaturQ lowers KL divergence to BF16 by 11--23\% relative to ModelOpt AutoQuantize at 4.2--6.0 effective bits, and it outperforms an interaction-aware allocator that measures up to 2{,}410 configurations while measuring only three. It also predicts the damage of unmeasured configurations with a median error of 6.9--11.4\%, lower than Gaussian-process and random-forest surrogates fit to 300 configurations, and served allocations of Qwen3.6-27B and GLM-5.2 (753B) run faster than vendor NVFP4 checkpoints at comparable accuracy.

title: Probabilistic "Copies" in Generative AI Models
summary:
Recent work shows that it is possible to extract verbatim or near-verbatim text of some copyrighted works from some large language models (LLMs or models). That is evidence that the model weights encode the works in some form---that the model has "memorized" those works from its training data. But LLMs don't store information in the same format as familiar databases. Rather, their weights store statistical relationships that have been learned from the training data, and those relationships inform a generation process that in practice is often probabilistic rather than deterministic. In the case of memorization, those relationships are strong enough that, in many circumstances, the model could generate a copyrighted work from its training data.
  Copyright law has not previously had to decide whether storing information that might or might not produce output similar to a copyrighted work is itself a copy of the work. The answer to this question is important, because it may determine the legality of many LLMs. The statute and caselaw are largely unhelpful. We argue that copyright law will likely take a functional approach to the question, finding that LLMs contain a copy of a particular work only if it is straightforward to extract that work in outputs. That result is unsatisfying as a policy matter, and we suggest potential changes to the law, but it is the most likely outcome under current law.

title: AlphaWiSE: Adaptive Weight Interpolation for Continual Multimodal Representation Learning
summary: Multimodal retrieval models align audio, images, and text in a shared embedding space, but sequential adaptation can degrade cross-modal relationships learned in earlier phases. Existing continual-learning procedures produce a single final checkpoint, so every retrieval direction shares the same stability-plasticity trade-off. We introduce AlphaWiSE, a post-hoc weight-space interpolation method that combines a sequential fine-tuning endpoint with a companion endpoint obtained with a stability-oriented continual-learning method. AlphaWiSE fits one scalar interpolation coefficient for each corresponding parameter tensor on an exemplar memory while both endpoints remain frozen. The interpolated tensors are then materialized into a single checkpoint, so the deployed model retains the architecture and inference cost of a single backbone. On continual audio-image-text retrieval, the fused model improves on the better of its two endpoints in 13 of 18 average retrieval measures and on the fixed blend of the same checkpoints in 25 of 36 measures. Its pairings achieve the strongest average audio-to-text and image-to-audio retrieval among all compared methods. Project page: https://alphawise.cvmlgroup.web.illinois.edu/

title: Enabling Spatially Fine-Grained DVFS in Neural Processing Units for Energy-Efficient LLM Serving
summary:
As neural processing units (NPUs) evolve rapidly to accommodate the ever-increasing compute demand of large language models (LLMs), their power consumption is becoming a limiting factor. Our study shows that using dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) to exploit the service-level objective (SLO) slacks is a promising way to improve NPU energy efficiency for LLM services. And as tensor operators in LLMs exhibit diverse bottlenecks across NPU components, it is desirable to configure the frequency separately for each component to maximize their energy efficiency.
  In this paper, we develop eNPU that enables hardware and software support for spatially fine-grained, component-level DVFS on NPUs. eNPU refactors the NPU core pipeline to partition components into separate V/$f$ domains. It introduces lightweight cross-domain communication mechanisms to mitigate synchronization overheads across components, and extends the NPU ISA for sub-$μ$s DVFS control. eNPU uses a compiler-driven two-level greedy search to co-optimize instruction scheduling and per-component V/$f$ selection under SLO constraints. We implement eNPU's pipeline design on an open-source NPU core to verify its functionality and evaluate the energy savings with a production-level NPU simulator with various LLMs using production traces. eNPU reduces energy consumption of LLM services by 25.8%--35.2% with 3.45% area overhead on a TPUv4 chip, while preserving strict SLO guarantees.

title: Auto-Scaling Heterogeneous Neural Processing Units for Energy and Cost-Efficient LLM Serving
summary:
To meet the ever-increasing computing demands of large language model (LLM) services, modern cloud platforms have widely deployed neural processing units (NPUs). These NPU chips have been developed and evolved at an incredibly fast pace, this inevitably produces heterogeneous compute pools backed by different versions of NPU chips. Unfortunately, due to the lack of system and architecture support for managing NPU heterogeneity in the cloud, it is unclear how to best utilize heterogeneous NPUs to maximize the energy and cost efficiency for LLM services.
  In this paper, we first conduct a characterization study of various generations of real NPU chips to demonstrate the potential benefits on energy/cost efficiency and performance by utilizing heterogeneous NPU chips. To realize these benefits, we present NeuScale, an auto-scaling framework to automatically exploit heterogeneous NPUs for cloud platforms. NeuScale manages heterogeneous NPU resources with a new vPod abstraction, which abstracts the core hardware parameters of different NPU versions and provides compatibility with existing ML frameworks. It makes the best-fit vPod allocations for different LLM inference requests using an intuitive and lightweight roofline-based analysis. It supports fine-grained dynamic NPU resource provisioning by adjusting both the vPod configuration (i.e., scaling up/down) and the number of vPods (e.g., scaling in/out). To validate the benefits of NeuScale at scale, we implement it with a production-level NPU simulator. Our evaluation with popular LLMs shows that NeuScale can significantly improve cost efficiency and service-level objective (SLO) satisfaction rate by best utilizing heterogeneous NPU resources.

title: A Multi-Center Dataset and Benchmark for SYNTAX Segmentation of Coronary Angiograms
comments: Accepted to WACV 2027 Dataset available on Zenodo at https://zenodo.org/records/19958730, code available at https://github.com/cvlab-ai/cardiag-benchmark
summary: Dense pixel-level classification of coronary angiography is essential for automated cardiovascular diagnostics, yet the computer vision community lacks gold-standard protocols and robust datasets to tackle this topologically complex, heavily long-tailed domain. To bridge this gap, we introduce CARDIAG: a rigorous, multi-center benchmark dataset designed to evaluate deep learning architectures on fine-grained SYNTAX segment classification. Unlike prior efforts, CARDIAG systematically prevents patient- and center-level data leakage while providing an unprecedented suite of annotations: highly imbalanced multi-class labels, explicit catheter and stenosis masks, expert uncertainty maps, temporal sequence frames, and spatial metadata. Using CARDIAG, we conduct the most extensive architectural sweep in this domain, benchmarking 24 models spanning classic CNNs, Vision Transformers (ViTs), and State-Space Models (SSMs). Moving beyond naive overlap metrics, we evaluate topological preservation (clDice), vessel diameter error, and uncertainty error-detection. Our analysis reveals an insight: modern large-kernel CNNs (particularly ConvNeXt V2 with DeepLabV3+) still outperform recent ViTs and SSMs under a shared training recipe, establishing a Dice = 0.456. By ensembling complementary models, we push the baseline to Dice = 0.479. Through leave-one-center-out cross-validation and data efficiency analyses, we explore the current limits of out-of-distribution generalization. Ultimately, CARDIAG establishes a foundation for advancing medical computer vision for cardiology across many downstream tasks, including lesion detection, temporal frame interpolation, and 3D reconstruction.

title: Set-defined graph classes: $χ$-boundedness meets tropical algebra
summary:
We study set-defined graph classes: hereditary classes whose vertices are assigned fixed-length numerical tuples, with adjacency determined solely by equality patterns among coordinates. These classes arise in structural graph theory, communication complexity, logic, and adjacency labeling schemes. We ask when they are $χ$-bounded, that is, when chromatic number is bounded in terms of clique number throughout the class.
  First, we prove a decomposition theorem: every graph in a set-defined class can be partitioned into a number of parts polynomially bounded in its clique number, each inducing a union of a bounded number of shift-colorable graphs, that is, graphs admitting a homomorphism to a shift graph. Thus bounded unions of shift-colorable graphs form the fundamental obstruction to $χ$-boundedness in set-defined classes.
  For full set-defined classes, consisting of all graphs realizable by a fixed Boolean rule on equality patterns, we prove a stronger dichotomy: every such class is either polynomially $χ$-bounded or contains the class of $D$-dimensional shift graphs for some $D \geq 2$. Moreover, we provide an algorithm that, given a Boolean-function description of a full set-defined class, decides $χ$-boundedness of the class. It reduces the problem to feasibility of tropical linear programs, and its correctness follows from a duality with winning strategies in mean-payoff games. Conversely, every integer system of tropical inequalities, and hence every mean-payoff game, can be encoded in strongly polynomial time as a set-defined class whose non-$χ$-boundedness is equivalent to feasibility. This provides a graph-theoretic counterpart of tropical feasibility and mean-payoff-game solvability, linking structural graph theory, tropical algebra, and game-theoretic algorithms.

title: HistoGPA: A Context-Conditioned Gene-Prior Attention Framework for Histology-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction
comments: 12 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables. v2: revised method description, added capacity-matched ablations, and updated abstract and appendix
summary: Spatial transcriptomics is costly, motivating the prediction of spatial gene expression from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) slides. Existing methods use tissue context to refine visual features but keep pretrained gene priors fixed across specimens. Since the relevance of such a prior may vary with tissue context, we propose HistoGPA, which conditions the gene prior itself on the slide being analyzed. A slide-level histological representation modulates a memory of pretrained gene embeddings before each spatial location queries it through cross-attention, and also gates context into the local features. Across ten cancer-specific tasks from HEST-1k, HistoGPA achieves a macro-averaged gene-wise Pearson correlation of 0.300 on the HEST-Bench genes, compared with 0.260 for the strongest of four recent methods. Capacity-matched ablations demonstrate the importance of slide-specific information and show that conditioning the gene prior provides benefits beyond visual context modulation, while pretrained gene embeddings outperform random tokens.

title: CogRec: Structure-Cognitive Fast-and-Slow Reasoning for Generative Recommendation
summary: Generative recommendation reformulates next-item prediction as identifier sequence generation, yet existing methods mainly treat the generated identifiers as target sequences to be memorized, leaving their hierarchical and relational structure underused for explicit reasoning. We propose CogRec, a structure-cognitive fast-and-slow reasoning framework that grounds intermediate reasoning in the same SID topology used for target generation. CogRec augments the vertical SID hierarchy with intra-layer semantic graphs and introduces SID Routing to represent recommendation reasoning through layer-wise Match, LateralJump, and Explore operations. These operations provide a structural interpretation of fast localization and slow navigation. A supervised multi-stage pipeline aligns newly introduced SID tokens, establishes direct generation, and trains natural-language and SID Routing branches from a shared checkpoint. Experiments on three Amazon Reviews 2014 categories show dataset-dependent effects of SID Routing. Routing improves Hit@10 and NDCG@10 over its direct-generation counterpart on Beauty and Sports, while reducing both metrics on Toys. These results characterize the benefits and dataset-dependent behavior of SID-grounded intermediate reasoning for generative recommendation. Code is available at https://github.com/caskcsg/CogRec.

title: Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in recommendation systems
summary: Large-scale recommendation systems face "Memory Wall" bottlenecks due to massive, dense embedding tables. While generative retrieval uses discrete tokens for IDs, high-dimensional context still relies on inefficient dense formats. Inspired by computer vision data compression, we propose Dual-purpose Semantic IDs to achieve LLM-level I/O efficiency. Our methodology uses hierarchical quantization to condense continuous embeddings into discrete Semantic IDs performing two concurrent roles: (1) Collaborative Identity: modeling user-item interactions via learnable embedding table; and (2) Content Reconstruction: using a lightweight Semantic Decoder for on-the-fly embedding approximation. This approach replaces massive vector storage with on-demand reconstruction, reducing system overhead and data footprints. We demonstrate the efficacy of our framework through offline evaluations and successful online deployment in production-scale ranking and retrieval systems at a major video sharing platform, showing that discrete tokens are indeed all you need for highly efficient, content-rich recommendation.

title: Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot Traces at Production Scale
summary: AI coding agents (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Codex) interleave multi-step LLM inference with tool execution, creating a workload different from chatbots. We present the first production-scale characterization of coding agents using sampled GitHub Copilot traces from June-July 2026, comprising 7.4M users, 819M conversations, 5.7B LLM calls, and 946T tokens. Our analysis reveals distinctive workload properties with unique systems implications: e.g., sparse user-initiated turns unfold into autonomous agent loops with nearly 1:1 coupling between LLM calls and tool execution; parallel LLM calls are rare but exist in turns that trigger subagents; KV cache hit rates average 90% within a turn, but fall to 52% across turn boundaries and to 6% after model switches; workflows and user behaviors exhibit diverse, long-tailed resource footprints. We further distinguish short agentic turnaround times from minutes-long user idle periods between turns, and develop a lightweight idle-time predictor that captures 87-89% of total idle time. We demonstrate two use cases: (1) a harness-side LLM API keep-alive policy that preserves provider-side context KV cache, reducing token costs by 14.9% on turn boundaries; and (2) a serving-side KV cache residency policy that uses predicted idle time to guide DRAM offloading, reducing time to first token (TTFT) by 3-33% compared with LRU during a one-week evaluation with GitHub Copilot traces.

AI.title_translation: 野外智能体编码：大规模生产环境中GitHub Copilot追踪的特征分析
AI.tldr: 本文对大规模生产环境下的GitHub Copilot代理编码轨迹进行了首次表征，揭示了其独特的工作负载特性和系统影响，并提出了两种优化方案以降低成本和提高性能。
AI.motivation: AI编码代理（如GitHub Copilot）的工作负载与传统聊天机器人不同，它们交织多步LLM推理和工具执行。为了更好地理解这种新型工作负载并优化相关系统，需要对其进行生产规模的特征分析。
AI.method: 研究团队使用2026年6月至7月GitHub Copilot的抽样追踪数据（包含7.4M用户、8.19亿对话、5.7B LLM调用和946T token）进行了首次生产规模的编码代理特征分析。他们分析了工作负载属性，并开发了一个轻量级空闲时间预测器。在此基础上，提出了两种优化方案并进行了演示：一种是LLM API保活策略，另一种是KV缓存驻留策略。
AI.result: 分析揭示了独特的工作负载特性，例如：用户发起的稀疏轮次会展开成自主代理循环，LLM调用与工具执行几乎1:1耦合；并行LLM调用很少见，但存在于触发子代理的轮次中；KV缓存命中率在轮次内平均为90%，但跨轮次边界降至52%，模型切换后降至6%；工作流和用户行为表现出多样化、长尾的资源占用。研究区分了短的代理周转时间与数分钟长的用户轮次间空闲时间，并开发了一个轻量级空闲时间预测器，捕捉了总空闲时间的87-89%。演示了两种用例：(1) 一种Harness-side LLM API保活策略，可保留提供商侧上下文KV缓存，在轮次边界将token成本降低14.9%；(2) 一种Serving-side KV缓存驻留策略，使用预测的空闲时间指导DRAM卸载，在为期一周的GitHub Copilot追踪评估中，与LRU相比，将首次token时间（TTFT）减少了3-33%。
AI.conclusion: 本文首次对生产规模的AI编码代理（GitHub Copilot）工作负载进行了详细的特征分析，揭示了其独特的系统行为和性能瓶颈。基于这些发现，研究提出了有效的优化策略，例如API保活和智能KV缓存管理，显著降低了成本并提高了响应速度，为未来AI编码代理系统的设计和优化提供了宝贵的见解。
AI.translation: AI编码代理（例如GitHub Copilot、Claude Code、Codex）将多步大型语言模型（LLM）推理与工具执行交织在一起，产生了与聊天机器人不同的工作负载。我们首次对生产规模的编码代理进行了特征分析，使用了2026年6月至7月GitHub Copilot的抽样追踪数据，其中包括740万用户、8.19亿次对话、57亿次LLM调用和946万亿token。我们的分析揭示了独特的工作负载属性及其独特的系统影响：例如，稀疏的用户发起轮次会展开成自主代理循环，LLM调用与工具执行之间几乎是1:1的耦合；并行LLM调用很少见，但存在于触发子代理的轮次中；KV缓存命中率在轮次内平均为90%，但在跨轮次边界时降至52%，在模型切换后降至6%；工作流和用户行为表现出多样化、长尾的资源占用。我们进一步区分了代理周转时间短与用户轮次之间长达数分钟的空闲时间，并开发了一个轻量级空闲时间预测器，捕捉了总空闲时间的87-89%。我们展示了两个用例：(1) 一种Harness-side LLM API保活策略，可保留提供商侧上下文KV缓存，在轮次边界将token成本降低14.9%；(2) 一种Serving-side KV缓存驻留策略，使用预测的空闲时间指导DRAM卸载，在为期一周的GitHub Copilot追踪评估中，与LRU相比，将首次token时间（TTFT）减少了3-33%。
AI.summary: 本文对GitHub Copilot在生产环境中的代理编码工作负载进行了首次大规模特征分析，基于2026年6月至7月的海量追踪数据。研究揭示了AI编码代理独特的系统行为，如LLM调用与工具执行的紧密耦合、KV缓存命中率在不同场景下的显著差异以及长尾资源占用。在此基础上，论文提出了一个空闲时间预测器，并演示了两种优化策略：通过API保活降低token成本14.9%，以及通过智能KV缓存管理减少首次token时间3-33%，为AI编码代理的系统设计和性能优化提供了重要指导。
AI.keywords: AI编码代理, GitHub Copilot, 工作负载特征, KV缓存, 性能优化
AI.comments: 该论文首次对生产规模的AI编码代理（如GitHub Copilot）工作负载进行了深度剖析，填补了该领域的数据空白。其创新之处在于通过大规模数据分析揭示了这类系统独特的工作负载模式和潜在的系统瓶颈。提出的空闲时间预测器和基于此的优化策略（API保活与智能KV缓存管理）具有重要的实践价值，能够显著提升效率并降低成本。这对于未来设计和优化AI编码工具的底层系统具有指导意义，特别是对LLM推理服务提供商而言，提供了宝贵的性能优化方向。

title: BODHI: Do LLMs Branch Out and Discover Heterogeneous Inferences?
summary: Although reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has improved the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs), whether it expands reasoning capabilities or primarily improves sampling efficiency remains debated. In this paper, we investigate the nature of test-time exploration in RLVR-trained LLMs by employing controlled maze-solving experiments and BODHI-TREEs, a reusable representation that groups mathematical reasoning segments based on semantic equivalence. These probes help delineate preferences between stylistic variations and semantically distinct continuations. We show that RLVR-trained models exhibit lower candidate preference entropy between semantically distinct continuations than their distilled counterparts, and complementary sampling experiments show lower empirical semantic entropy and fewer observed branches under equal sampling budgets. Thus, policy concentration extends beyond stylistic choices and reduces observed semantic diversity. This reduction coexists with improved constraint adherence and backtracking in mazes, and improved recovery from distracting steps in mathematical reasoning. We conjecture that improved trace validity drives RLVR's sampling-efficiency gains, while policy concentration reduces rollout diversity. Our findings identify a central challenge for RLVR: preserving diverse reasoning trajectories alongside improved trace validity.

AI.title_translation: BODHI：大型语言模型是否会分岔并发现异质推理？
AI.tldr: RLVR提高了LLM的推理性能，但通过集中策略减少了推理路径的多样性，这在提高采样效率的同时也带来了保持多样性的挑战。
AI.motivation: 探讨强化学习与可验证奖励（RLVR）训练的大型语言模型（LLMs）是否真正扩展了推理能力，还是主要提高了采样效率。
AI.method: 采用受控迷宫求解实验和BODHI-TREEs（一种基于语义等效性对数学推理片段进行分组的可重用表示）来调查RLVR训练LLM在测试时的探索性质。
AI.result: RLVR训练的模型在语义上不同的延续之间表现出比其蒸馏对应物更低的候选偏好熵，且在相同的采样预算下，观察到的语义熵和分支更少。策略集中超出了风格选择，并减少了观察到的语义多样性。这种减少与迷宫中改进的约束遵守和回溯以及数学推理中从干扰步骤中恢复能力的提高并存。
AI.conclusion: 改进的轨迹有效性推动了RLVR的采样效率增益，而策略集中则减少了推出多样性。RLVR面临的核心挑战是：在提高轨迹有效性的同时，如何保持推理轨迹的多样性。
AI.translation: 尽管带有可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）提高了大型语言模型（LLMs）的推理性能，但它是否扩展了推理能力或主要提高了采样效率仍存在争议。在本文中，我们通过采用受控迷宫求解实验和BODHI-TREEs（一种基于语义等效性对数学推理片段进行分组的可重用表示）来调查RLVR训练的LLMs在测试时的探索性质。这些探测器有助于区分风格变异和语义上不同的延续之间的偏好。我们发现，RLVR训练的模型在语义上不同的延续之间表现出比其蒸馏对应物更低的候选偏好熵，并且互补的采样实验表明，在相同的采样预算下，观察到的语义熵更低，分支更少。因此，策略集中超出了风格选择，并减少了观察到的语义多样性。这种减少与迷宫中改进的约束遵守和回溯以及数学推理中从干扰步骤中恢复能力的提高并存。我们推测，改进的轨迹有效性推动了RLVR的采样效率增益，而策略集中则减少了推出多样性。我们的发现指出了RLVR的一个核心挑战：在提高轨迹有效性的同时，如何保持推理轨迹的多样性。
AI.summary: 本文研究了RLVR训练的LLM在测试时的探索行为。通过迷宫求解和BODHI-TREEs分析，发现RLVR导致策略集中，减少了语义多样性。尽管这提高了约束遵守和问题恢复能力，但同时也降低了推理路径的多样性。研究指出，RLVR的核心挑战在于在提高轨迹有效性的同时，如何保持推理轨迹的多样性。
AI.keywords: 大型语言模型, 强化学习, 推理多样性, 策略集中, 采样效率
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过实验揭示了RLVR在提高LLM推理性能时的一个重要权衡：虽然它通过策略集中提高了采样效率和问题解决的准确性，但却牺牲了推理路径的多样性。这对于理解RLVR的工作机制及其未来发展方向具有重要意义，尤其是在需要创造性或多视角推理的场景中，如何平衡效率和多样性将是一个关键研究点。

title: Flying over The Uncertain Nature (FORTUNE): Intelligent and Humanistic 3D Path Planning for Low-Altitude Collaboration
summary: Low-altitude intelligent agents are driving demand for timely, socially responsible collaborative sensing in dynamic urban environments. Yet jointly handling heterogeneous spatio-temporal sensing demands, real-time uncertainty, and human-centered constraints in a unified multi-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) framework remains challenging. We study 3D multi-UAV path planning and joint task assignment under heterogeneous spatio-temporal uncertainty of ground points of interest (PoIs). Unlike studies assuming static, known PoIs, we formulate a unified model capturing persistent (Type-I), temporally predictable (Type-II), and emergent unpredictable (Type-III) demands. Following the low-altitude-for-good principle, we explicitly model altitude-dependent societal and environmental costs, including noise and public safety risks, jointly optimizing sensing effectiveness and socially compliant operations. To solve the resulting large-scale mixed-integer nonlinear problem, we propose FORTUNE, a hierarchical offline-online framework. Offline, a Transformer-based predictor forecasts Type-II activation windows, while an enhanced sparrow search algorithm (ES2A) with priority-aware decoding and danger-aware evolution generates globally coordinated flight plans. Online, lightweight trajectory refinement accommodates new Type-III PoIs while preserving global mission coherence. Experiments on real-world traffic and synthetic datasets show FORTUNE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks, validating effectiveness, scalability, and practical applicability in dynamic low-altitude systems.

AI.title_translation: 飞越不确定性本质（FORTUNE）：用于低空协同的智能与人文3D路径规划
AI.tldr: 本文提出了FORTUNE框架，通过结合Transformer预测和改进的麻雀搜索算法，解决了低空多无人机在动态环境中的三维路径规划与人文关怀协同问题。
AI.motivation: 现有的低空多无人机框架难以在统一模型中同时处理异构的时空感知需求、实时不确定性以及以人为本的约束（如噪音和公共安全风险）。
AI.method: 提出了一种名为FORTUNE的分层离线-在线框架：离线阶段利用基于Transformer的预测器预测时序可预测需求，并采用带有优先级感知解码和危险感知进化的增强麻雀搜索算法（ES2A）生成全局航迹；在线阶段则通过轻量级轨迹优化来适应突发不可预测需求。
AI.result: 在真实交通和合成数据集上的实验表明，FORTUNE在有效性、可扩展性和实际应用性方面均持续优于当前的最新基准。
AI.conclusion: FORTUNE框架成功实现了动态城市环境中多无人机的高效、社会友好的三维路径规划与任务分配，实验证明其优于现有基准方法。
AI.translation: 低空智能代理正在推动动态城市环境中及时且具社会责任感的协同感知需求。然而，在一个统一的多无人机（UAV）框架中，同时处理异构的时空感知需求、实时不确定性和以人为本的约束仍然具有挑战性。我们研究了在地面兴趣点（PoIs）异构时空不确定性下的3D多无人机路径规划和联合任务分配。与假设静态已知PoIs的研究不同，我们建立了一个统一的模型，捕捉持久性（I型）、时间可预测性（II型）和突发不可遵循性（III型）的需求。遵循“低空向善”原则，我们显式建模了与高度相关的社会和环境成本（包括噪音和公共安全风险），共同优化感知效率与社会合规操作。为了解决由此产生的规模化混合整数非线性问题，我们提出了FORTUNE，一个分层的离线-在线框架。离线状态下，基于Transformer的预测器预测II型激活窗口，同时采用具有优先级感知解码和危险感知进化的增强麻雀搜索算法（ES2A）生成全局协调的飞行计划。在线状态下，轻量级轨迹求精在保持全局任务连贯性的同时适应新的III型PoIs。在真实交通和合成数据集上的实验表明，FORTUNE consistently（持续地）优于最先进的基准，验证了其在动态低空系统中的有效性、可扩展性和实际适用性。
AI.summary: 该论文研究了动态城市环境中考虑异构时空不确定性和以人为本约束的多无人机三维路径规划与任务分配问题，并提出了FORTUNE分层框架，通过离线全局规划与在线动态调整相结合，实现了高效且社会友好的低空协同作业。
AI.keywords: 无人机路径规划, 任务分配, 低空经济, 不确定性处理, 人文关怀约束
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种兼顾智能化与人文关怀（社会及环境成本）的低空多无人机三维路径规划与任务分配框架，结合了Transformer预测与改进麻雀搜索算法，在动态低空系统中表现出良好的有效性和可扩展性。

title: SiMDex: Mining Similar Egocentric Videos for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation
comments: 38 pages, 12 figures, 16 tables. Project page: https://lin-nie.github.io/SiMDex/
summary: Recent years have witnessed an explosive trend of scaling ego-centric human videos for robot manipulation, yet it remains unclear which data actually benefits dexterous manipulation. We present SiMDex, a similarity-based data mining framework that casts human data selection for VLA post-training in dexterous manipulation as a recommendation problem. For each robot demonstration, SiMDex runs a recall-ranking-re-ranking cascade over ~32M egocentric human samples: two stages, recall and ranking, select a task-relevant subset in a morphology-agnostic action space, and re-ranking verifies it on pixels, with no change to VLA architecture or training. Against a strong baseline trained with an equal amount of randomly sampled human data, SiMDex uses only ~1.49M mined samples (<5% of the pool) yet improves the overall success rate from 47.7% to 61.7%, showing that selective curation outperforms indiscriminate data mixing.
comment: 38 pages, 12 figures, 16 tables. Project page: https://lin-nie.github.io/SiMDex/

AI.title_translation: SiMDex：挖掘相似的第一视角视频以实现跨具身灵巧操作
AI.tldr: SiMDex通过创新的数据挖掘框架，从海量人类第一视角视频中精准筛选出不到5%的优质数据用于机器人后训练，显著提升了跨具身灵巧操作的成功率。
AI.motivation: 近年来虽然有利用大规模主观视角人类视频进行机器人操作的趋势，但对于哪类数据真正对灵巧操作有益尚不明确，盲目混合数据效果不佳，因此需要一种高效的数据挖掘与筛选框架。
AI.method: 提出SiMDex框架，将人类数据选择构建为推荐问题，包含召回-排序-重排（recall-ranking-re-ranking）级联流程，在前两个阶段在形态无关的动作空间中选择任务相关的子集，并在像素级别进行重排验证。
AI.result: 使用约1.49M（占数据池的不到5%）由SiMDex挖掘的样本进行训练，使机器人的总体成功率从47.7%提升到了61.7%，显著优于使用同等数量随机采样人类数据的强基线模型。
AI.conclusion: SiMDex框架通过精心筛选一小部分（<5%）高度相关的主观视角人类视频数据，显著提升了机器人跨具身灵巧操作的成功率，证明了精细化数据筛选优于盲目的大规模数据混合。
AI.translation: 近年来，利用大规模第一视角人类视频进行机器人操作呈现出爆发式增长趋势，但究竟哪些数据真正有利于灵巧操作尚不明确。我们提出了SiMDex，这是一个基于相似度的数据针对灵巧操作中VLA后训练的人类数据选择构建为推荐问题的框架。对于每个机器人演示，SiMDex在约3200万个第一视角人类样本上运行召回-排序-重排级联：前两个阶段（召回和排序）在形态无关的动作空间中选择与任务相关的子集，而重排则在像素上进行验证，无需更改VLA架构或训练过程。与使用等量随机采样人类数据的强大基线相比，SiMDex仅使用约1.49M个挖掘样本（占数据池的不到5%），就将总体成功率从47.7%提高到61.7%，这表明选择性整理优于盲目数据混合。
AI.summary: SiMDex是一个基于相似度的数据挖掘框架，旨在为机器人灵巧操作的VLA模型后训练选择高质量的主观视角人类视频。通过召回-排序-重排的级联机制，该框架能从3200万个样本中精准筛选出不到5%的高价值数据，在无需改变VLA架构的前提下大幅提升了操作成功率。
AI.keywords: 跨具身灵巧操作, 主观视角视频, 数据挖掘, 视觉-语言-动作模型, 推荐系统
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种新颖且高效的基于相似度的数据挖掘框架，将人类数据选择转化为推荐问题，有效解决了机器人灵巧操作中跨具身人类视频利用率低、盲目混合数据效果差的问题，对大规模视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型的后训练具有重要的启发意义和应用价值。

title: Why Does CLAUDE.md Keep Growing? Catastrophic Remembering in Agentic Coding
summary: Agentic prompts like CLAUDE.md grow without bound in real repositories, stopping only when history ends or someone rewrites the file wholesale. We trace this to imperfect recall: appending an instruction is always cheap, but once an instruction's latent reasoning is gone, deleting it without risking a regression costs O(2^|D|) in a prompt of |D| instructions. Successive edits destroy that latent reasoning, additions outrun deletions and prompts grow until agents become non-functional -- catastrophic remembering. First, we characterize this phenomenon across 247,694 instruction lifetimes in 1,867 repositories: agentic prompts grow nearly monotonically, more than tripling over their lifetime (+226%) at +4.7 net instructions per commit. Deletion hazard decays geometrically with instruction age, consistent with imperfect recall and with no other rival we test. Then, we show that prompt comments can halt the growth: in verifiable worlds built by inverting IFEval, comments encoding latent reasoning remove 99.3% of excess size (+211.3% to +1.4%). Finally, we show comments yield smaller real-world and coding-convention prompts than existing context maintainers, grow more effective with model capability and, at small scale, improve instruction-following in real repositories by 17.7%. If English is the new code, why don't we have comments yet?

AI.title_translation: CLAUDE.md 为什么一直在膨胀？智能编程中的灾难性记忆
AI.tldr: 智能体编程中的提示词因“不完美召回”而无限增长导致失效，而引入类似代码注释的潜在推理机制可以有效解决这一膨胀问题。
AI.motivation: 探究为什么智能编程助手中的代理提示（如CLAUDE.md）在实际代码库中会无限制地增长，并找出解决这种“提示词膨胀”现象的方法。
AI.method: 分析了1,867个代码库中247,694个指令生命周期的增长模式；在基于IFEval构建的可验证世界中测试了提示注释的效果；并在真实代码库中评估了注释对提示维护和指令遵循的实际影响。
AI.result: 代理提示几乎单调增长，生命周期内增长超过三倍（+226%），平均每次提交净增4.7条指令；删除风险随指令年龄几何级衰减；引入编码潜在推理的注释减少了99.3%的超额大小，并在真实代码库中将指令遵循能力提升了17.7%。
AI.conclusion: 智能体编程中无限制的提示词增长源于不完美召回导致的“灾难性记忆”现象；引入编码潜在推理的提示注释可以有效阻止提示词无限膨胀，并提升指令遵循能力。
AI.translation: 诸如 CLAUDE.md 这样的智能体提示词在真实的仓库中无节制地增长，只有在历史结束或有人彻底重写该文件时才会停止。我们将此归因于不完美的回忆：追加一条指令总是成本低廉的，但一旦指令的潜在推理消失，在包含 $|D|$ 条指令的提示中，删除该指令而不承担回归风险的成本高达 $O(2^{|D|})$。连续的编辑破坏了这种潜在推理，添加的速度超过了删除的速度，提示词不断增长，直到智能体失去功能——这就是灾难性记忆。首先，我们在 1,867 个仓库的 247,694 个指令生命周期中对这一现象进行了特征分析：智能体提示几乎呈单调增长，在其生命周期内增长了三倍以上（+226%），平均每次提交净增加 4.7 条指令。删除危险随指令年龄呈几何级数衰减，这与不完美回忆一致，且与我们测试的其他任何竞争假设均不符。然后，我们证明了提示词注释可以阻止这种增长：在通过反转 IFEval 构建的可验证世界中，编码潜在推理的注释消除了 99.3% 的超额大小（从 +211.3% 降至 +1.4%）。最后，我们证明了与现有的上下文维护器相比，注释能够产生更小的真实世界和编码规范提示词，随着模型能力的增强变得更有效，并且在小规模下，能够将真实仓库中的指令遵循能力提高 17.7%。如果英语是新代码，为什么我们现在还没有注释？
AI.summary: 本文研究了智能编程提示词（CLAUDE.md）在实际代码库中无限增长的“灾难性记忆”现象。作者发现，由于不完美召回导致删除旧指令的风险随年龄呈指数级上升，促使提示词不断累加。通过在大规模真实代码库中分析和在受控世界中实验，作者证明引入解释潜在推理的“提示注释”可以有效停止提示词膨胀，减少冗余并提升智能体指令遵循能力。
AI.keywords: Agentic coding, CLAUDE.md, Prompt growth, Catastrophic remembering, Imperfect recall
AI.comments: 该论文敏锐地捕捉到了智能编程助手在实际应用中遇到的“提示词膨胀”问题，并提出了“灾难性记忆”这一新颖概念。通过理论分析和大规模数据验证，揭示了由于缺乏潜在推理导致指令难以安全删除的根本原因，并创新性地引入了类似代码注释的机制来解决这一问题。具有极高的工程实用价值和理论启发意义。

title: Towards Understanding On-Policy Distillation through the Lens of Test-Time Scaling
comments: 34 pages. Code and data: https://j3ra1d.top/opd-test-time-scaling/ Checkpoints: https://huggingface.co/collections/Geraldxm/opd-test-time-scaling-math-code-and-fact-checkpoints-6aba42275d3362d882cfc472
summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) has emerged as a promising post-training technique for enhancing LLM reasoning. Under the reverse KL objective, the idealized optimum of OPD aligns the student distribution with that of the teacher. When the teacher consistently outperforms the student, this naturally suggests that OPD should yield broad improvements over the pre-OPD student. However, do such improvements extend across the entire range of test-time sampling budgets? In this work, we revisit this expectation through the lens of test-time scaling by varying the sampling budget $K$ and evaluating performance with pass@$K$. Across multiple settings, we observe two distinct patterns: OPD can improve pass@$K$ at both small and large sampling budgets, but it can also improve small-budget performance while reducing large-budget pass@$K$. We show one condition that guarantees such a reversal and an idealized reverse KL counterexample where it occurs even when the teacher has higher accuracy on every problem. To choose between two candidate teachers at a target sampling budget, we propose the \textit{Teacher Advantage Score at $K$} (TAS@$K$), which can be computed before OPD training to predict which teacher will lead to a larger improvement in pass@$K$. Across three domains and thirteen benchmarks, the ordering predicted by TAS@$K$ agrees with the observed pass@$K$ improvements of the resulting OPD models in 83.6\% of experiments, providing a useful signal for teacher selection at the target pass@$K$.

AI.title_translation: 通过测试期扩展的视角理解在线策略蒸馏
AI.tldr: 本文发现在线策略蒸馏（OPD）在不同测试期采样预算下表现出复杂的性能变化，并提出了一种名为 TAS@$K$ 的指标来指导教师选择。
AI.motivation: 虽然理想状态下在线策略蒸馏（OPD）能使学生分布对齐教师，但这种提升是否能延伸至整个测试期采样预算范围尚不明确，因此需要从测试期扩展的视角重新审视这一期望。
AI.method: 通过在不同采样预算 $K$ 下利用 pass@$K$ 评估 OPD 的性能，并提出“在 $K$ 处的教师优势得分”（TAS@$K$）来预测教师选择效果。
AI.result: 研究发现 OPD 在小预算和大预算下表现出复杂模式（有时大预算性能会下降），并证明了导致该现象的条件；同时，提出的 TAS@$K$ 指标在 83.6% 的实验中成功预测了最佳教师。
AI.conclusion: 作者通过测试期扩展的视角揭示了在线策略蒸馏（OPD）在不同采样预算下的性能表现差异，并提出了有效的教师选择指标 TAS@$K$，对提升大模型后训练效果具有重要价值。
AI.translation: 在线策略蒸馏（OPD）已成为增强大语言模型推理能力的一种有前景的后训练技术。在反向 KL 目标下，OPD 的理想最优解是将学生分布与教师分布对齐。当教师持续优于学生时，这自然表明 OPD 应该在预 OPD 学生的基础上带来广泛的改进。然而，这种改进是否会延伸到测试期采样预算的整个范围？在这项工作中，我们通过改变采样预算 $K$ 并使用 pass@$K$ 评估性能，从测试期扩展的视角重新审视了这种期望。在多种设置中，我们观察到两种截然不同的模式：OPD 可以在小采样和大采样预算下都提高 pass@$K$，但也可能提高小预算性能同时降低大预算的 pass@$K$。我们展示了一个保证这种反转发生的条件，以及一个理想的反向 KL 反例——即使教师在每个问题上的准确率都更高，这种情况也会发生。为了在目标采样预算下的两个候选教师之间进行选择，我们提出了“在 $K$ 处的教师优势得分”（TAS@$K$），它可以在 OPD 训练之前计算，以预测哪个教师会带来更大的 pass@$K$ 改进。在三个领域和十三项基准测试中，由 TAS@$K$ 预测的排序与所得 OPD 模型的观测 pass@$K$ 改进在 83.6% 的实验中保持一致，为目标 pass@$K$ 下的教师选择提供了有用的信号。
AI.summary: 本文从测试期扩展的视角研究了在线策略蒸馏（OPD），发现 OPD 并不总能在所有采样预算下提升性能，并提出了 TAS@$K$ 这一有效的教师选择指标。
AI.keywords: On-policy distillation, Test-time scaling, LLM reasoning, Teacher selection
AI.comments: 本文通过测试期扩展（test-time scaling）的视角重新审视了在线策略蒸馏（OPD），发现OPD并不总能在所有采样预算下带来性能提升，甚至可能出现小预算提升、大预算下降的反常现象。作者为此提出了预测指标 TAS@$K$，在多个领域和基准测试中表现出很高的预测准确率，具有重要的实践指导意义。

title: Massive Activations in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models: Pre-Attention Spikes and Inter-Spike Plateaus
summary: We present the first systematic study of massive activations (MAs) in layer-interleaved Hybrid linear attention large language models (HLA LLMs), examining their architectural organization, training-time emergence, underlying mechanisms, and functional significance. Across five linear attention architectures, six hybridization configurations, and five input domains, we identify two architecture-aligned morphologies: pre-attention spikes (PAS) immediately before full attention and inter-spike plateaus (ISP) persisting through intervening linear attention layers. Denser full attention increasingly connects PAS through ISP, approaching the persistent MAs of conventional Transformers. This organization also recurs across 12 public checkpoints spanning 1.2B-397B parameters, covering linear attention and state-space hybrids. Controlled pretraining of Gated DeltaNet (GDN) hybrids up to 1.3B reveals early emergence and consolidation of both morphologies, alongside asymmetric gating effects. Specifically, full attention output gates strongly attenuate MA magnitudes without eliminating their organization, whereas removing GDN output gates yields modest amplification. Mechanistically, we develop a shared systematic-outlier account: PAS follows a localized write-sink-cancel process, while ISP is consistent with delayed cancellation. Functionally, our interventions show that deleting only the four largest-magnitude PAS coordinates at each full attention input reduces mean downstream accuracy by 21.9%-63.6% relative to normal inference. Moreover, reference-conditioned spike-to-plateau connection consistently improves mean real-world retrieval accuracy, yielding relative gains of 1.1%-12.6% without retraining. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/Massive-Activations-HLA.

AI.title_translation: 混合线性注意力大语言模型中的巨激活：预注意力尖峰与尖峰间高原
AI.tldr: 本文首次系统研究了混合线性注意力大语言模型中的巨激活现象，发现了独特的预注意力尖峰和层间高原形态，揭示了其产生机制及对模型性能的核心作用。
AI.motivation: 旨在填补对层交错混合线性注意力大语言模型（HLA LLMs）中巨激活（MAs）现象研究的空白，探讨其架构组织、训练时涌现、底层机制及功能意义。
AI.method: 跨越5种线性注意力架构、6种混合配置、5个输入领域以及12个公开检查点进行系统性实证分析；对Gated DeltaNet混合模型进行高达1.3B参数的受控预训练；实施激活删除和干预实验。
AI.result: 发现了两种架构对齐的巨激活形态：预注意力尖峰（PAS）和层间高原（ISP）；明确了门控机制对巨激活的调控作用；证明了PAS对下游准确性的关键作用，以及利用spike-to-plateau连接提升真实世界检索准确性的效果。
AI.conclusion: 混合线性注意力大语言模型中存在特征鲜明的巨激活形态（PAS和ISP），它们对模型的准确性和信息检索能力至关重要，且受门控机制的显著调控。
AI.translation: 我们对层交错混合线性注意力大语言模型（HLA LLMs）中的巨激活（MAs）进行了首次系统研究，考察了它们的架构组织、训练时涌现、底层机制和功能意义。在5种线性注意力架构、6种混合配置和5种输入领域中，我们识别出两种与架构相对应的形态：紧接在全注意力之前的预注意力尖峰（PAS）以及贯穿干预线性注意力层的层间高原（ISP）。更密集的全注意力通过ISP越来越多地连接PAS，逼近传统Transformer的持久MAs。这种组织形态也在涵盖1.2B至397B参数、跨越线性注意力和状态空间混合的12个公开检查点中重复出现。对高达1.3B参数的Gated DeltaNet（GDN）混合模型的受控预训练揭示了这两种形态的早期涌现和巩固，以及不对称的门控效应。具体而言，全注意力输出门显著减弱了MA的幅度但未消除其组织结构，而移除GDN输出门则产生适度的放大。在机制上，我们提出了一个共享的系统性异常值解释：PAS遵循局部的写-汇聚-抵消过程，而ISP与延迟抵消一致。在功能上，我们的干预表明，在每个全注意力输入处仅删除四个最大幅度的PAS坐标，就会使平均下游准确率相对于正常推理下降21.9%-63.6%。此外，条件参考的spike-to-plateau连接持续提高了平均现实世界的检索准确率，在无需重新训练的情况下产生了1.1%-12.6%的相对增益。我们的代码可在 https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/Massive-Activations-HLA 获取。
AI.summary: 该论文首次系统研究了混合线性注意力大语言模型中的巨激活现象，识别出PAS和ISP两种关键形态，揭示了其机制、门控影响及对模型性能和检索能力的重要功能。
AI.keywords: 巨激活, 线性注意力, 大语言模型, 混合架构, 门控机制
AI.comments: 本文首次系统地研究了混合线性注意力大型语言模型（HLA LLMs）中的巨激活（MAs）现象，揭示了其独特的形态、演化机制及功能重要性，为理解和优化新型大语言模型架构提供了宝贵的视角。

title: SYSEVOLVE: Safe, Autonomous Attack-Defense Co-evolution for Evolving Cyber Defense
comments: Technical Report For SysEvolve System, version 261120
summary: The offensive capability of large language models (LLMs) has crossed from research demonstration into documented reality. Frontier models have autonomously breached real production systems, and open-weight models now deliver frontier-level exploitation at negligible cost. Existing defenses cannot keep pace with such attacks: human-intensive defense updates over days to weeks, while AI-based defense, on the other side, trained on fixed historical data, does not adapt to an evolving attacker. We trace these persistent failures to one root cause: defense evolves in isolation, cut off from the adversary that should be driving its evolution. That isolation manifests at three layers: the deployment layer, the capability layer, and the adversarial layer. To build a defense that evolves at the speed of attack, we propose co-evolution as the integrating insight, replacing isolated evolution with mutual driving between attack and defense. Based on this insight, we present SysEvolve, a safe and autonomous co-evolutionary system built from three co-designed components, SysField, SysSpear, and SysArmor. SysField constructs realistic multi-host ranges via declarative topology-driven construction. SysSpear generates efficient, safe attack schemes via task-sliced local search, a bidirectional expert-knowledge base, and static-analysis verification. SysArmor performs real-time, interpretable defense via state tracking, CTI-context fusion, and stage-matched response. In evaluation, SysField achieves zero-loss collection at 2.1\% overhead and orchestrates 257 CVEs into 1,148 ranges. SysSpear improves red-team success by over 25\%, attains the best completion on complex multi-vulnerability ranges. SysArmor achieves 10--1000$\times$ greater precision than prior systems and detects real APT attacks in production at Huawei and Sangfor. Our evaluation also reveals four findings about LLM agent capabilities.
